text:
cora-support: Hey @alice-sre — customer AcmeCorp (private/VPC) is blocked pulling packages and model artifacts after onboarding. They see failures for apt/pip and model registry pulls. Can you confirm egress allowlist entries we need?

cora-support: Repro steps they provided:
```
# from an onprem worker inside their VPC
curl -v https://registry.redwood-internal.io/v2/_catalog
* About to connect() to registry.redwood-internal.io port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.20.30.40... connected
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30001 milliseconds with 0 out of 0 bytes received
```

cora-support: apt/pip errors (truncated):
```
Err:1 http://mirror.pkg.redwood-cdn.net/ubuntu bionic/main amd64 Packages
  Could not connect to mirror.pkg.redwood-cdn.net:443 (10.20.30.50), connection timed out
WARNING: Retrying (Retry(total=4, connect=None, read=None, redirect=None, status=None)):
  Could not fetch https://files.pythonhosted.org/... SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED
```

cora-support: They said their security team only allows explicit egress allowlists (no proxy wildcard), and they can't rely on IPs alone because infra is NATed. They asked for exact hostnames + ports and any CIDR hints.

alice-sre: Thanks @cora-support. First quick checks for them to run if possible:
- `dig +short registry.redwood-internal.io` -> verify DNS resolves to expected egress NAT IP not an internal blackhole.
- `openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-internal.io:443 -servername registry.redwood-internal.io` (shows cert chain and SNI behavior).
- check firewall logs for DENY to destination port 443 for those NAT IPs.

alice-sre: Also ask security team if they perform TLS interception (corporate MITM). If a TLS proxy re-signs certs our token exchange to auth.redwood.ai will fail with CERT_VERIFY_FAILED.

ben-devops: Here's the minimal allowlist we typically ask customers to add for Private deployments (TCP 443 unless noted):
- registry.redwood-internal.io
- models.redwood.ai
- packages.redwood.ai (apt/pip mirrors / CDN front)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (443 outbound for metrics/heartbeats)
- auth.redwood.ai (token exchange / oauth)
- files.pythonhosted.org (pypi)
- pypi.org
- deb.nodesource.com (node packages)
- storage.googleapis.com (object pulls for model shards)
- mirror.pkg.redwood-cdn.net

ben-devops: We avoid recommending IPs since CDNs/Cloud providers rotate. If they insist on IP ranges, ask which cloud region they're in and we can provide ASN/range hints (e.g., Cloudflare/Cloudfront or GCS ranges).

diego-support: FYI — a lot of customers hit the same issue when their TLS inspection modifies SNI or re-signs certs. Workarounds:
- Add SNI passthrough exceptions for the FQDNs above in the TLS proxy.
- If not possible, temporarily host model artifacts in an internal artifact bucket and point the deployment config to use local urls (we can help with a short-lived rollback).
- For package installs: set `Acquire::http::Proxy`/`pip --trusted-host` is a hack but meh.

deploy-bot: New internal ticket created: INF-2147 — "Customer egress allowlist request: AcmeCorp (Private)". Assigned: eng-sre. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INF-2147

cora-support: Thanks all — I'll send the FQDN list + ports to AcmeCorp security and ask them to confirm when entries are in place. If they still see CERT_VERIFY_FAILED after allowlist, I'll collect `openssl s_client -showcerts` output and firewall deny logs and reopen the ticket. :thumbsup:
